name: Firestore (Firebase)
summary: Firestore is a hosted database from Google that stores app data as documents and keeps it instantly synced across users.

free_plan_covers.note: Free Spark plan: 1 GiB storage, 50,000 reads, 20,000 writes, and 20,000 deletes per day.

first_paid_usd_month.note: The paid Blaze plan has no flat monthly fee; it only charges for usage beyond the free daily quotas.

portability.note: Firestore uses Google's own document API and query model, so moving to another database needs real rework.

storage_model.note: Google runs and manages Firestore for you in the cloud.

data_model.note: Firestore stores data as JSON-like documents grouped into collections.

realtime_built_in.note: Live listeners push document and query changes straight to connected apps; this is a core, documented feature.

serverless_friendly.note: The SDK makes lightweight calls instead of holding fixed connections, avoiding connection-limit problems in serverless functions.

mobile_sdk.note: Official SDKs cover iOS, Android, and Flutter; React Native works through a widely used community package instead.

setup.step: Create a Firebase project at the Firebase console.
Register a web app in the project to get your Firebase config values.
Install the Firebase SDK in your Next.js app.
In the console, create a Firestore database and choose a starting security mode.
Add the Firebase config values to your app. Firebase's docs do not require environment variables, but NEXT_PUBLIC_ names are a common Next.js convention.

builder_notes: New databases start open to everyone or closed to everyone; write real Firestore Security Rules before shipping.
The web config values (apiKey, etc.) are safe to ship in browser code; they are not secret. Real protection comes from Security Rules.
For server-side writes that must bypass rules, use the Admin SDK with a service account key kept only in server environment variables, never sent to the browser.
